topic: PM Modi Became India's Longest Continuously Serving Elected PM

subtopics.title: Appointment, Tenure and the Council of Ministers
subtopics.summary: The President appoints the PM but is not free in the selection, and normally invites the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha to form the government. If no single party has a clear majority, the President invites a person likely to command support of two or more parties that make up a Lok Sabha majority. The PM holds office during the pleasure of the President but cannot be dismissed while enjoying majority support in the Lok Sabha. Rules for the Council of Ministers include a 15% size cap and a six-month limit for ministers who are not in Parliament.
facts: The President normally invites the leader of the majority party to form the government.
If no single party has a clear majority, the President invites a person who can command support of two or more parties forming a Lok Sabha majority.
The PM is normally the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha.
Some Members of the Rajya Sabha have been made Prime Minister.
The PM holds office during the pleasure of the President.
The President cannot dismiss the PM while he enjoys majority support in the Lok Sabha.
If the PM loses the confidence of the Lok Sabha, he must resign or the President can dismiss him.
The salary and allowances of the PM are determined by Parliament.
The size of the Council of Ministers cannot exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha (91st Amendment, 2003).
A minister who is not in Parliament for six months will lose their position.
Article 88 allows ministers to take part in both Houses but does not guarantee them voting rights.

subtopics.title: Modi's Firsts and Records in Context
subtopics.summary: Modi is the first Indian PM born after 15 August 1947 and the longest-serving PM from outside the Indian National Congress. He is among the few Indian PMs to secure three consecutive electoral mandates at the Union level. In 2014, the BJP-led NDA won an absolute majority of 336 out of 543 Lok Sabha seats, which the booklet calls the first Non-Congress single party majority government.
facts: Modi is the first Indian PM born after 15 August 1947.
Modi is the longest-serving PM from outside the Indian National Congress.
Modi is among the few Indian PMs to secure 3 consecutive electoral mandates at the Union level.
Modi is the 3rd PM after Nehru and Indira Gandhi to serve 3 terms.
In 2014, the BJP-led NDA got an absolute majority of 336 out of 543 Lok Sabha seats.
The 2014 government is described as the first Non-Congress single party majority government.
The BJP became the first party since 1984 to get a majority in the Lok Sabha.
Morarji Desai was India's first Non-Congress PM and its oldest PM at 81 years.
Rajiv Gandhi was India's youngest PM at 40 years.
V.P. Singh was the first PM to leave office following a no-confidence vote.
